paragraphs: DFloat11 reduces the memory needed to store large language and diffusion models while preserving their outputs bit for bit. Its starting observation is that BFloat16 weights contain statistical redundancy: the representation uses more space than the information in those weights requires. The method exploits this redundancy through entropy coding, assigning variable-length encodings according to frequency.

Making compressed weights useful during inference also requires decoding them quickly. The authors develop a GPU decompression kernel with compact lookup tables that fit in fast on-chip memory. A two-phase procedure coordinates where threads read and write, while decompression operates at transformer-block granularity to limit latency.

Experiments report roughly 30% smaller models with identical outputs. Against uncompressed models that offload weights to the CPU to fit memory constraints, token throughput improves by 2.3–46.2 times. Under fixed GPU memory, generation lengths increase by 5.7–14.9 times. The method also enables lossless inference of the 810GB Llama 3.1 405B model on eight 80GB GPUs in one node.
neurips-2025-70-size-100-accuracy-lossle.tldr: DFloat11 compresses model weights by about 30% and decompresses them efficiently on GPUs while preserving bit-for-bit identical outputs.

paragraphs: This paper asks how the first stages of mouse vision can support recognition when contrast and brightness change. The researchers build a differentiable biophysical model containing 200 cone photoreceptors, horizontal cells, and bipolar cells. Its components include mechanisms for converting light into electrical signals, releasing neurotransmitters, and controlling cell activity through cell-specific ion channels.

The model combines two sources of constraint. Cone parameters are fitted to measurements of electrical responses and synaptic release. The larger retinal circuit is then trained on visual classification with changing contrast and luminance. This connects measured cellular behavior with a functional task, allowing the researchers to examine how different cell populations contribute.

The model learns classification despite those variations and generalizes to unseen contrast levels better than a linear classifier. In the tested configurations, adding horizontal-cell feedback does not improve performance beyond photoreceptors and bipolar cells. These findings show how modeled retinal nonlinearities can support contrast-tolerant classification, while locating the horizontal-cell result within this particular model and task.
neurips-2025-a-data-and-task-constrained.tldr: A biologically grounded mouse-retina model learns contrast-tolerant classification, with no additional task benefit from horizontal-cell feedback in the tested configurations.

paragraphs: AgentTTS addresses how to spend inference compute on tasks composed of several different stages. Each stage may benefit from a different language model and a different amount of computation. The objective is to choose these jointly so that the complete task performs well, rather than treating every stage as an independent allocation problem.

This search is difficult because the number of model-and-budget combinations grows rapidly, and evaluating a combination requires costly inference. Choices also interact across stages. The authors first conduct pilot experiments on four tasks across six datasets, identifying three empirical patterns that inform their approach. AgentTTS then uses a language-model agent to revise allocations through repeated interactions with the execution environment and feedback from those interactions.

The reported experiments show significantly better search efficiency than traditional and other language-model-based baselines. They also show greater robustness to changes in training-set size and improved interpretability. The contribution is a feedback-driven way to search for effective compute allocations across an entire workflow.
neurips-2025-agenttts-large-language-mod.tldr: AgentTTS uses an LLM agent and execution feedback to search efficiently for model choices and compute budgets across multi-stage tasks.

paragraphs: This paper examines when data augmentation can help estimate causal effects and generalize across interventions. Its central condition is that an augmentation leaves the mechanism generating the outcome unchanged. Under that condition, the augmentation can be interpreted as changing the mechanism that assigns treatment, potentially reducing bias caused by unobserved confounders.

The authors connect this idea to instrumental variables, which provide a source of treatment randomization but may be difficult to obtain. They introduce IV-like regression by regularizing instrumental-variable estimators. The aim is to mitigate confounding and improve prediction across interventions even when some instrumental-variable properties are relaxed. Parameterized augmentations can then be expressed within this framework.

The paper further shows how composing augmentations can simulate a worst-case application of them, improving causal estimation and generalization beyond simple augmentation. Support includes population-level theory, finite-sample simulations using a simple linear example, and real-data experiments. The outcome-invariance condition is essential to the proposed interpretation; the argument does not apply indiscriminately to every data transformation.
neurips-2025-an-analysis-of-causal-effec.tldr: Outcome-preserving augmentations can act like interventions on treatment assignment and potentially improve causal estimation through IV-like regression.

paragraphs: Language models receive instructions with different levels of authority, but they do not always respect that ordering when directives conflict. This becomes particularly difficult during multi-step reasoning, where an early mistake can affect later steps. The paper develops training supervision that checks whether a model follows the appropriate directive without requiring a supplied ideal answer or reasoning trace.

Each synthesized example contains a directive to follow, a conflicting directive, and an executable checker. That checker deterministically evaluates whether the output meets the intended requirement. The data-generation pipeline includes unit tests, language-model-assisted repairs, and a probabilistic analysis of how reliably its cleaning process removes problems. The same supervision framework supports both instruction-tuned and reasoning models.

Fine-tuning with these examples improves adherence to instruction hierarchy and robustness on safety evaluations. The gains transfer to adversarial safety benchmarks without supervision tailored to those tasks. The findings support verifiable output checks as a scalable training signal for handling conflicting instructions, with evidence extending beyond the synthesized training instances.
neurips-2025-beyond-oracle-verifier-supe.tldr: Executable verifiers provide supervision for instruction conflicts, improving hierarchy adherence and safety robustness without oracle answers or reasoning traces.

paragraphs: BNMusic aims to make environmental noise less noticeable by incorporating its acoustic character into personalized music. Conventional masking covers unwanted noise with another sound, but mismatched rhythms can require large volume increases. This work instead generates music that fits the noise and follows a user's text description of the desired music.

The framework has two stages. First, it produces a complete musical piece in a mel-spectrogram representation, incorporating the musical qualities of the environmental sound. Second, it adaptively increases the volume of the generated segment to strengthen the blend while preserving auditory quality. Rhythmic alignment and amplification therefore work together to reduce how much the noise stands out.

Evaluations on MusicBench, EPIC-SOUNDS, and ESC-50 support the effectiveness of this approach. The authors report enjoyable music segments that align with environmental noise and reduce its noticeability. The intended improvement is perceptual: the surrounding noise becomes part of a more coherent listening experience through music generation and adaptive volume adjustment.
neurips-2025-bnmusic-blending-environmen.tldr: BNMusic generates personalized, rhythmically aligned music that blends with environmental noise to make it less noticeable.

paragraphs: Choosing the proportions of different pretraining data sources can substantially affect language-model performance. Testing many mixtures at full scale is expensive, while extrapolating from small experiments can depend on brittle assumptions. This paper introduces a probabilistic approach that explicitly represents uncertainty when using inexpensive experiments to guide larger training decisions.

The framework treats data curation as sequential Bayesian optimization. At each step, it chooses a data mixture, model size, and training duration, balancing experimental cost against the information an experiment could provide. Considering these choices together allows noisy results from smaller or shorter runs to inform which expensive runs are worth pursuing.

The authors build a simulator from 472 pretraining runs with different SlimPajama mixtures. Across model sizes from 20 million to one billion parameters, even simple components yield useful decisions. They report speedups of 2.6 times over multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization and 3.3 times over random search. These results demonstrate potential efficiency gains from accounting for uncertainty and scale jointly when searching for training-data mixtures.
neurips-2025-data-mixture-optimization-a.tldr: A Bayesian framework jointly selects data mixtures, model sizes, and training durations to guide expensive pretraining decisions using cheaper experiments.

paragraphs: DrivAerStar provides simulation data for learning accurate, faster predictions of vehicle aerodynamics. Reducing aerodynamic drag matters for electric-vehicle range and energy use, but detailed fluid simulations can make design iterations take weeks. The paper targets dataset shortcomings that impede industrial use, including coarse computational meshes, omitted vehicle components, and discrepancies with physical validation.

The dataset contains 12,000 STAR-CCM+ simulations covering three vehicle configurations. Shapes vary through 20 CAD parameters using free-form deformation. The simulations include engine compartments, cooling systems, and internal airflow. Refined meshes and strict control of the near-wall resolution measure y-plus help capture the flow behavior needed for accurate aerodynamic analysis.

The authors report wind-tunnel validation error below 1.04%, described as a fivefold improvement over existing datasets. Benchmark models trained on DrivAerStar achieve accuracy the paper characterizes as production-ready while reducing computational costs from weeks to minutes. The contribution connects detailed engineering simulations with machine-learning development through a dataset designed around industrial modeling requirements.
neurips-2025-drivaerstar-an-industrial-g.tldr: DrivAerStar supplies 12,000 detailed vehicle-flow simulations to support machine-learning models with industrially relevant aerodynamic accuracy.

paragraphs: FFN Fusion investigates whether parts of a language model that normally execute in sequence can run in parallel with little effect on accuracy. The main opportunity appears in sequences of feed-forward network layers, especially after particular attention layers have been removed. Reducing these sequential dependencies can shorten the time needed to produce a model response.

The authors develop a method for identifying suitable layer sequences and fusing them into parallel operations. The key claim is qualified: such sequences can often be parallelized while largely preserving behavior. This makes the choice of which layers to combine a central part of the technique, rather than assuming all sequential computation is interchangeable.

Applied to Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct, the techniques produce a 253-billion-parameter model called 253B-Base. The paper reports a 1.71-fold inference-latency speedup and 35-fold lower per-token cost while retaining strong benchmark performance. It also finds that complete transformer blocks can sometimes be parallelized, suggesting further architectural possibilities beyond feed-forward layers alone.
neurips-2025-ffn-fusion-rethinking-seque.tldr: FFN Fusion parallelizes suitable sequences of language-model layers to reduce inference latency while largely preserving model behavior.

paragraphs: Decision-tree learning often improves an existing tree through small local changes. This paper studies two kinds of change: adjusting a split threshold, or changing the feature used by a split as well. The objective is to minimize classification errors using a fixed number of operations of one chosen type.

The authors show that the resulting optimization problems are NP-complete in general, then examine which characteristics account for that difficulty. A small number of features alone does not make the problems tractable, and neither does a small feature-domain size alone. Together, however, these restrictions permit a fixed-parameter algorithm, giving a more precise account of when local improvement can be computed efficiently.

The stated running time is (D + 1)^(2d) multiplied by a polynomial in input size, where d counts features and D measures domain size. Thus, the exponential dependence is concentrated in those two parameters. A proof-of-concept implementation and empirical results accompany the theory, connecting the tractability analysis to an executable approach for improving trees.
neurips-2025-improving-decision-trees-th.tldr: Local decision-tree improvement is NP-complete generally but becomes fixed-parameter tractable when feature count and domain size are jointly bounded.

paragraphs: IndEgo is a dataset for studying assistants that understand industrial work from a worker's viewpoint and from external cameras. It covers activities such as assembly, disassembly, logistics, inspection, repair, and woodworking. A central emphasis is collaboration: two workers jointly carry out tasks that demand both physical effort and reasoning.

The collection includes 3,460 first-person recordings totaling approximately 197 hours, plus 1,092 external-view recordings totaling about 97 hours. First-person recordings combine contextual signals such as gaze, narration, audio, and motion. Annotations describe actions, summaries, mistakes, and narrations, while processed outputs include hand poses, gaze information, and semi-dense three-dimensional point clouds.

The authors also provide benchmarks for procedural and non-procedural task understanding, mistake detection, and reasoning-based question answering. Baseline evaluations show that mistake detection, question answering, and collaborative task understanding remain challenging for leading multimodal models. The dataset therefore supplies both varied observations of industrial work and structured ways to measure whether models understand the activities and interactions they observe.
neurips-2025-indego-a-dataset-of-industr.tldr: IndEgo combines first-person and external recordings of industrial collaboration with rich annotations and challenging multimodal understanding benchmarks.

paragraphs: Computational imaging systems process sensor measurements before, or instead of, showing them to a person. This makes the information carried by those measurements especially important. The paper develops a way to quantify how much noisy measurements reveal about unknown objects, using mutual information rather than visual appearance or performance on a particular downstream task.

The method fits probabilistic models to the measurements and their noise characteristics. These models provide an estimate that upper-bounds the true mutual information, so the quantity is a bound rather than an exact measurement. The authors then optimize these estimates with gradients in a design method called Information-Driven Encoder Analysis Learning, or IDEAL.

Across color photography, radio astronomy, lensless imaging, and microscopy, the estimates accurately reflect differences in system performance. Systems designed with IDEAL match those designed by jointly optimizing imaging hardware and processing algorithms. The findings support mutual information as a broadly applicable criterion for evaluating imaging systems and guiding computationally efficient design.
neurips-2025-information-driven-design-o.tldr: IDEAL designs imaging systems by optimizing an upper-bound estimate of the information their noisy measurements contain about objects.

paragraphs: PartCAD reconstructs editable CAD instructions from a point cloud, a collection of points describing three-dimensional geometry. The goal includes recovering a modeling sequence that represents how a shape can be constructed. This connects observed geometry to design operations, making the result useful for reverse engineering and CAD automation.

The framework first processes the point cloud autoregressively, building representations organized around individual parts. These representations serve as interpretable anchors for generation. A second component uses projections onto three planes to provide explicit geometric cues about design intent. Finally, a non-autoregressive decoder produces sketch and extrusion parameters in one forward pass, supporting efficient generation of structurally coherent instructions.

The separation between sequential part reasoning and single-pass parameter generation is central to the approach. It combines awareness of the object's components with an efficient final decoding stage. Experiments report significantly higher accuracy and robustness than existing CAD instruction-generation methods. The findings support part-oriented geometric reasoning as a way to recover editable models from point-cloud observations.
neurips-2025-learning-cad-modeling-seque.tldr: PartCAD combines part-aware representations and three-plane projections to reconstruct accurate, robust, editable CAD instructions from point clouds.

paragraphs: This paper studies how softmax normalization limits an attention mechanism's ability to select informative tokens. It develops a theoretical framework that relates selection to the geometry of token representations. Explicit bounds describe distances and separation conditions under softmax scaling, providing a way to analyze when token vectors remain distinguishable.

The authors test their theoretical findings using a pretrained GPT-2 model. They report that selecting more tokens weakens the model's ability to distinguish informative ones, often pushing attention toward a more uniform selection pattern. The word 'often' matters: the reported behavior is a tendency in the analysis and experiments, rather than a claim that every attention distribution must become uniform.

The paper also identifies gradient-sensitivity difficulties associated with softmax normalization, particularly at low temperatures. This connects the selection problem to training behavior as well as the geometry of token representations. Together, the findings motivate more robust normalization and selection mechanisms for future attention architectures, while providing theoretical and empirical tools for understanding the existing mechanism.
neurips-2025-limitations-of-normalizatio.tldr: Theory and GPT-2 experiments reveal weaker token discrimination as selection expands and gradient-sensitivity challenges under low-temperature softmax normalization.

paragraphs: MIRA is a foundation model designed to forecast medical measurements over time. Such data often arrive at irregular intervals, use different sampling rates, and contain missing observations. The paper addresses these characteristics directly, with the broader motivation of reducing the customization and annotation needed when models transfer across medical datasets and tasks.

Three components handle different aspects of time. Continuous-time rotary positional encoding represents fine differences between observation times. A frequency-specific mixture of experts routes computation among specialists for different temporal patterns. A neural differential-equation block models how hidden states evolve continuously, allowing forecasts at arbitrary requested timestamps rather than only a fixed sequence of times.

MIRA is pretrained on publicly available medical datasets totaling more than 454 billion time points. The authors report average forecasting-error reductions of 8% in out-of-distribution settings and 6% in in-distribution settings. They also introduce a benchmark spanning several downstream clinical tasks. The results support this architecture's ability to forecast heterogeneous medical time series across the evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-mira-medical-time-series-fo.tldr: MIRA combines continuous-time modeling and frequency specialization to improve forecasting of irregular medical time series.

paragraphs: Dynamic graphs change in two interacting ways: the features of their nodes evolve, and connections between nodes can change. Graph Neural Controlled Differential Equations model these temporal paths on graph domains. This paper builds on that approach by incorporating permutation equivariance, a symmetry that makes the model respond consistently when nodes are relabeled.

The proposed method projects Graph Neural CDEs into a space of functions with that symmetry. Relabeling a graph should relabel the corresponding representation in the same way. Restricting the model to this function space substantially reduces its parameter count, while the authors report that it retains representational power. The architectural constraint therefore provides a route to greater efficiency without sacrificing the stated modeling capability.

Experiments cover simulated dynamical systems and real-world tasks. They show more efficient training, improved generalization, and better performance in both interpolation and extrapolation scenarios. The findings support using graph symmetry directly in continuous-time representation learning, especially when the objective includes learning temporal behavior that extends beyond the observed examples.
neurips-2025-permutation-equivariant-neu.tldr: Permutation-equivariant Graph Neural CDEs reduce parameter counts while preserving representational power and improving empirical temporal generalization.

paragraphs: PipeFusion targets the latency of generating high-resolution images with diffusion transformers. It distributes work along two dimensions: image patches and model layers. These pieces are scheduled as a pipeline across multiple GPUs, coordinating computation with communication so that distributing the model does not require excessive data exchange.

The method uses the similarity between inputs at consecutive diffusion steps. Feature maps from the preceding step provide context for the current pipeline step, even though they are one step old. Reusing this context reduces communication relative to tensor parallelism, sequence parallelism, and DistriFusion. Distributing model parameters across devices also improves memory efficiency, which matters for large diffusion transformers such as Flux.1.

Experiments on eight L40 GPUs connected through PCIe report state-of-the-art performance for Pixart, Stable Diffusion 3, and Flux.1. These results demonstrate the benefits of combining patch scheduling, layer distribution, and reused features in the evaluated hardware setting. The core opportunity comes from exploiting similarity between diffusion steps when arranging work across GPUs.
neurips-2025-pipefusion-patch-level-pipe.tldr: PipeFusion pipelines image patches and model layers across GPUs, reusing previous-step features to reduce diffusion-transformer communication and latency.

paragraphs: The Riemannian Proximal Sampler generates samples from probability densities defined on curved spaces called Riemannian manifolds. Its operation depends on two mathematical subroutines, or oracles: one for Brownian increments on the manifold and another for its heat kernel. The accuracy of these subroutines is central to the sampling guarantees.

With exact oracles, the authors prove that reaching error epsilon requires a number of iterations growing as log(1/epsilon), measured using Kullback–Leibler divergence. With sufficiently accurate approximate oracles, the guarantee becomes log-squared in 1/epsilon under total variation distance. These are separate conditional results with different error measures, so the oracle assumptions belong alongside the rates.

The paper also presents practical oracle implementations using truncated heat kernels and Varadhan's asymptotic approximation. Under the latter approach, it connects the sampler to a discretized entropy-regularized proximal optimization method on a Wasserstein space. Preliminary numerical results illustrate effectiveness. The contribution combines high-accuracy theory with concrete approximations for the operations that theory requires.
neurips-2025-riemannian-proximal-sampler.tldr: A manifold sampler achieves high-accuracy iteration guarantees conditional on exact or sufficiently accurate Brownian-increment and heat-kernel oracles.

paragraphs: ROOT studies how to find high-performing inputs to a black-box function using only a fixed collection of observed input-output pairs. Common approaches either optimize a learned approximation of the function or generate inputs conditioned on a desired output. Both face a bottleneck when the available observations are limited.

The paper reframes the task as translating between distributions. A probabilistic bridge learns to transform a distribution of low-value inputs into one containing high-value candidates. To train this bridge, the method constructs synthetic functions intended to resemble the target function. These come from posterior means of Gaussian processes fitted to the offline data with different parameterizations, providing additional low- and high-value training examples.

This makes the synthetic functions a central link between the limited observations and the learned transformation. The authors evaluate ROOT on an extensive benchmark including recent methods and report significant improvements and state-of-the-art performance. The results support distributional translation as an effective alternative formulation for the evaluated offline optimization problems.
neurips-2025-root-rethinking-offline-opt.tldr: ROOT learns a probabilistic transformation from low-value to high-value inputs using synthetic functions derived from fixed offline observations.

paragraphs: SignFlow Bipartite Subgraph Network predicts whether links have positive or negative signs in graphs connecting two groups of nodes. Such graphs appear in social and recommendation settings, but learning from their structure can become costly at large scales. The method addresses both training memory and the cost of making predictions after training.

During its first stage, a heuristic extracts neighborhoods around the links being predicted. Directed message passing then gathers the local structural patterns useful for sign prediction. Working with these smaller subgraphs supports sublinear growth in training memory. However, repeatedly extracting subgraphs would still make prediction inefficient, so the method adds a second stage.

That stage distills information learned from subgraphs into node features, allowing fast inference while retaining rich structural information. Experiments on medium- and large-scale datasets report superior predictive performance alongside efficient memory and computation use. The contribution is the combination of detailed local learning during training and a more economical representation for subsequent prediction.
neurips-2025-signflow-bipartite-subgraph.tldr: SBSN learns link signs from local subgraphs, then distills their structural information into node features for fast large-scale inference.

paragraphs: Structural causal bandits use knowledge of causal relationships to narrow an agent's action choices. If the known structure rules out an action as a possible reward maximizer, the agent can avoid exploring it. The existing framework assumes access to a fully specified causal diagram, making the completeness of causal knowledge a central requirement.

This paper relaxes that requirement by working with a Markov equivalence class, where the available structural information corresponds to a class of causal graphs. The agent receives this information as a partial ancestral graph, or PAG. The framework must therefore identify potentially optimal actions while respecting uncertainty in the causal structure supplied to it.

The authors propose a generalized procedure for identifying those potentially optimal actions within the PAG. Its contribution is to extend structural action pruning to a less fully specified form of causal knowledge. The resulting scope is broader: an agent can use partial structural information to reason about which actions remain candidates for maximizing reward.
neurips-2025-structural-causal-bandits-u.tldr: This framework extends causal-bandit action pruning from fully specified causal diagrams to partial ancestral graphs representing Markov equivalence classes.

paragraphs: This paper investigates a physical vulnerability in traffic-sign recognition using fluorescent ink as the medium for an adversarial patch. The proposed FIPatch is intended to be less conspicuous than visible stickers or projections. Its effect depends on fluorescence activated by ultraviolet illumination, which can cause the recognition system to assign an incorrect sign label.

The researchers model the fluorescence effect digitally before evaluating it physically. This links the simulated appearance change to the real-world behavior of the material. The contribution centers on the interaction between the sign's surface, illumination, and machine recognition, showing how a physical change can affect classification even when the attack medium is designed for stealth.

The reported evaluation achieves a 98.31% attack success rate in low-light conditions. The authors also report bypassing five popular defenses with a success rate of 96.72%. These findings document effectiveness under the evaluated conditions, with low light explicitly qualifying the first result. The work identifies fluorescence as a relevant physical failure mode for traffic-sign recognition systems.
neurips-2025-the-fluorescent-veil-a-stea.tldr: FIPatch uses ultraviolet-activated fluorescent ink to induce traffic-sign recognition errors, reporting high success in low-light evaluations and against tested defenses.

paragraphs: This paper studies how language models organize knowledge within the parameters of their multilayer perceptrons, or MLPs. Its motivation is efficient use of a limited parameter budget: performance may depend on how stored knowledge is arranged and accessed, as well as on how many parameters the model has.

The researchers analyze twenty publicly available open-source language models. They find that models with stronger knowledge capabilities show greater parameter specialization. In particular, MLP parameters tend to concentrate on similar types of knowledge. This identifies a relationship between model capability and the internal organization of knowledge across parameters, providing a more detailed perspective on what stronger models have in common.

The work then goes beyond that comparison through experimental validation and causal training experiments. The authors report that specialized knowledge distributions improve how efficiently models use stored knowledge and play a critical role in that efficiency. The findings therefore support specialization as a contributing mechanism in the examined models, alongside its observed association with stronger knowledge capabilities.
neurips-2025-the-rise-of-parameter-speci.tldr: Analysis of twenty language models and causal training experiments links MLP parameter specialization to more efficient use of stored knowledge.

paragraphs: Adafactor is a memory-efficient optimizer that approximates second-moment information with a rank-one matrix factorization and removes first-order momentum. This greatly reduces auxiliary storage compared with maintaining full optimizer statistics. The paper addresses a theoretical gap: understanding convergence when these compressed statistics interact with the algorithm's update-clipping mechanism.

The authors analyze smooth, non-convex optimization and establish rates for reaching stationary points, where gradients vanish or become small. The rates are optimal up to logarithmic factors in both deterministic and stochastic settings, with sub-Gaussian noise assumed in the stochastic case. The guarantee concerns stationary points rather than a claim of finding a global optimum.

The analysis treats Adafactor as an approximation to Adam. A new proxy step size captures the adaptive behavior arising from factorization and clipping, while an induction argument controls gradient magnitudes. The results suggest that rank-one approximation of Adam's second-moment matrix need not fundamentally impair convergence. This supplies theoretical support for a memory-saving design already motivated by large-scale training.
neurips-2025-theoretical-investigation-o.tldr: Adafactor attains near-optimal stationary-point convergence rates for smooth non-convex optimization, including stochastic settings with sub-Gaussian noise.

paragraphs: Tropical Attention introduces a mathematical structure intended to suit combinatorial reasoning. It moves the attention kernel into tropical projective space, where computation is piecewise linear and has a 1-Lipschitz property that controls sensitivity. This preserves sharp, polyhedral decision regions associated with combinatorial problems, providing an architectural bias toward their structure.

The authors prove that stacks of multi-head Tropical Attention can universally approximate tropical circuits and implement tropical transitive closure through composition. These constructions have polynomial resource bounds and do not require recurrent mechanisms. The guarantees explain properties of the represented computations, including sharp and scale-invariant decision boundaries.

Experiments report stronger generalization to unfamiliar lengths and values, robustness to perturbative noise, and substantially faster inference with fewer parameters relative to the stated Softmax and recurrent baselines. The work also extends its neural algorithmic reasoning study to NP-hard and NP-complete problems. That empirical scope is distinct from the polynomial resource guarantees for the specific tropical constructions proved in the paper.
neurips-2025-tropical-attention-neural-a.tldr: Tropical Attention uses piecewise-linear geometry to support combinatorial reasoning, with theoretical representation guarantees and improved empirical generalization and robustness.
